name: Horseshoe Bend National Military Park
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Horseshoe Bend National Military Park in east-central Alabama preserves the site of the decisive battle of the Creek War. On March 27, 1814, forces led by General Andrew Jackson, including U.S. Army regulars, Tennessee militia, Cherokee allies, and Lower Creek warriors, attacked the fortified camp of the Red Stick Creek faction at a horseshoe-shaped bend on the Tallapoosa River. Approximately 800 of the 1,000 Red Stick warriors were killed in the battle — one of the deadliest defeats suffered by Native Americans in U.S. history. The resulting Treaty of Fort Jackson forced the Creek Nation to cede roughly 23 million acres — half of present-day Alabama and part of southern Georgia — to the United States. The park was established in 1956.
